item.content:encoded:
Same as Act I — comments as I go.

Chapter 4:

  • Ohh hey, Carter already? Be still my heart! Heh, this feels sorta quick, but since the story isn't exactly short, I don't mind. My reaction was basically "Oh cool!"
  • Somehow I missed that Jeremy was Marshall. This may be my fault. However, I really like him as Marshall.
  • I already like Carter. Neat character.
  • Why does Edward feel revulsion? I actually don't get it — this is a surprisingly charming Carter (even though there's the underlying creepy element).
  • "Marshall, seeing Edward's bewildered expression, interjected to return the conversation to something approximating sanity." > POV shift here — this is Marshall's POV, not Edward's. I'd rephrase.
  • I'm surprised by how much I like Carter and dislike Edward's 'cool' reaction (along with his earlier revulsion). I mean, he's still creepy, but c'mon. Not necessarily a problem with the story, btw. This scene was basically great.
  • Back in skim territory with the exposition from Edward's bosses, but I'm not sure it's a problem in this case. The details may be necessary for certain readers, and it feels realistic like they would go on at this length.
  • "Edward sat, gobsmacked by David Went's audacity. " > Normally I don't like it when you do this statement of the obvious, but it works in this case — I'm honestly just as gobsmacked. In a good way! Though… Edward really should have thought this through more! It just seems so odd that he misses so much. Sigh. Although at least it's consistent.
  • "Edward sat for a while looking at it. Did everyone involved with Marshall's little club get this special treatment? Or was this a warning?" > Good thought. He's actually thinking ahead of me as the reader — good. Also ups the tension & intrigue level.
  • The seashore dance is really cool — it's stretching to figure out how people could see this as non-anomalous, but you make it work — I believe it.
  • The nude sardines game is also a good idea, especially the strange inhuman woman in the dark.
  • Oh fuck. Didn't see this chapter-ending twist coming.

Chapter 5:

  • Fascinated by this scenario.
  • Amused by the detail of the lawyers and the phlegm.
  • I really don't like that he throws up because that detail is so overused, but in this case I'll give it a pass because I believe it here (it's usually not believable). I'd feel sick after all that buildup and with that reveal too.
  • It bugs me hilariously that "Acts238" gets it so wrong. There are not five horsemen — there are always only five, it's just that the makeup differs — but it fits in just fine that some random dude would get it wrong, so it still works okay.
  • "911truther" is too on-the-nose, though. I don't really believe it, and it makes it worse that this guy is the one who gives the info. I'd change the name. I'm slightly iffy on his dialogue, too, and that Edward so easily finds out this info, but… eh, I'm willing to roll with it.
  • Wait, wait, I misunderstood — the Four Horsemen really ARE just nerdy hackers, or posing as them? Okay, I believe that he could track them down, then. May be an information-flow-to-reader issue, not sure. Could just be me.
  • I'm sorta disappointed that they're this cliche, though… it's believable, but eh. Fun setup though. The Sprite sentence in particular is funny.
  • …though ultimately, you don't get enough out of them. They're pretty 'eh'.
  • I like that he's now paying attention to oddness surrounding him — I don't like that he didn't think of MC&D potentially tailing him before. But eh.
  • I like the chess thing.
  • Also like the comb.
  • "the presence" — oh shit — neat —
  • Good description of this scene.
  • Called this final twist or something like it happening. Not a bad thing, by the way — it's neat. Wondering how it will play out.

Overall: A very, very good second entry — outdoes the first, IMO. Excellent work.
